steps.what: Read the current security procedures and policies.
Decide which standards the procedure must state.
Develop procedure v1 for those security procedures.
Document procedure v1 as the filed security standard.

tasks.design: She reads the current procedures, decides the standards, develops procedure v1, and documents it. She still opens the current procedures. No listing replaces that reading, and no model writes the procedure.
tasks.previous_blocker: What the procedure must say is a judgement about this site.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new develops or documents the security procedure for her.
tasks.still_hard: A procedure she has not judged can still be wrong for this site.
tasks.human_edge: She can refuse a rule that does not match the practice she read.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. She still reads the procedures, decides the standards, develops procedure v1, and documents it.

reach.task: follow the security procedure she documented
reach.learn: The procedure is one she wrote, not a generated rule.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: she still reads the procedures, decides the standards, develops procedure v1, and documents it. No tool is added.

assumptions: The upkeep allowance is zero because no tool is added.
This performance is one visitor-access procedure. A patrol standard uses the same reading, deciding, developing, and documenting. One episode is that procedure.
She writes procedure v1 herself. The writing step is not gated. On the document step she checks that procedure v1 states the standards she chose. Filing is internal.
She still opens and reads the current procedures. No listing replaces that reading. No model drafts the procedure. No alert is raised.
unknowns: Whether an outside insurer must receive the filed procedure.
research_questions: Who else may change procedure v1 after she has filed it.

incremental.description: No upkeep, because no tool is added to this task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On one visitor-access procedure she reads the current procedures, decides the standards, develops procedure v1, and documents it, and none of those steps is shorter, so the saving stays at zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read which emergencies, such as fires, bombs, and other threats, need a drill.
Decide the date for that training or those drills.
Schedule the training or drills and write schedule v1.
File schedule v1 for those emergency drills.
Tell the staff the time of those drills.

tasks.design: She reads which emergencies need a drill, chooses the date, writes schedule v1, files it, and tells the staff. She still opens the notes and still speaks to the staff. No listing replaces that reading, and no alert is raised.
tasks.previous_blocker: Which date the site can spare is a judgement she makes with the people on duty.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new picks the date or runs the drill for her.
tasks.still_hard: A drill on a date the site cannot spare still fails.
tasks.human_edge: She can move the date because she knows who is on duty.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. She still reads the threats, chooses the date, writes and files the schedule, and tells the staff.

reach.task: attend the drill at the time she set
reach.learn: The time is one she chose and told them, not a generated roster.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: she still reads the threats, chooses the date, writes and files the schedule, and tells the staff. No tool is added.

assumptions: The upkeep allowance is zero because no tool is added.
This performance is one fire drill. A bomb drill uses the same reading, choosing, writing, filing, and telling. One episode is that drill.
She writes schedule v1 herself. The writing step is not gated. On the file step she checks that schedule v1 states the date she chose. Filing is internal.
Staff are colleagues. Telling them the time is spoken. No drill notice is sent, so the telling is not gated.
She still opens and reads the emergency notes. No listing replaces that reading. No alert is raised. Telling the fire service is not this task.
unknowns: Whether the fire service must be told the drill date on another task.
research_questions: Who can cancel the drill after she has told the staff.

incremental.description: No upkeep, because no tool is added to this task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On one fire drill she reads the threats, chooses the date, writes schedule v1, files it, and tells the staff, and none of those steps is shorter, so the saving stays at zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: See which items, such as keys and key cards, she will hand over.
Decide which persons may take those items.
Hand the key cards to those persons.
Write key log v1 for the items distributed.
File key log v1 for the items distributed.

tasks.design: She sees the key card, decides who may take it, hands it over, writes key log v1, and files it. She still looks at the card and still hands it over. No listing replaces that look, and no alert is raised.
tasks.previous_blocker: Whether this person may hold the key is a judgement at the desk.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new hands over the key or writes the log for her.
tasks.still_hard: A key handed to the wrong person is still out.
tasks.human_edge: She can refuse the key because she sees who is asking.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. She still sees the item, decides, hands it over, writes the log, and files it.

reach.task: return the key card she logged
reach.learn: The log names a card she handed over, not a generated entry.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: she still sees the item, decides who may take it, hands it over, writes key log v1, and files it. No tool is added.

assumptions: The upkeep allowance is zero because no tool is added.
This performance is one key card handed to one person. A key uses the same seeing, deciding, handing, writing, and filing. One episode is that hand-over.
She writes key log v1 herself after the hand-over. The writing step is not gated. On the file step she checks that key log v1 names the person and the card she handed over. Filing is internal.
Handing over the card writes nothing and is not a send. She still looks at the card. No listing replaces that look. No alert is raised.
unknowns: Whether a lost-card report sits on another task.
research_questions: Who may void key log v1 after she has filed it.

incremental.description: No upkeep, because no tool is added to this task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On one key card she sees the item, decides who may take it, hands it over, writes key log v1, and files it, and none of those steps is shorter, so the saving stays at zero.

steps.what: Decide the amounts for this department budget.
Write department budgets as budget v1.
File budget v1 for the department.
Present budget v1 to upper management or other stakeholders.

tasks.design: She reads last year's budgets, decides the amounts, writes budget v1, files it, and presents it to upper management. She still opens the figures and still speaks in the room. No listing replaces that reading, and no alert is raised.
tasks.previous_blocker: Which amounts the department can defend is a judgement she makes.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new writes the budget or presents it for her.
tasks.still_hard: A figure she cannot explain still fails in the room.
tasks.human_edge: She can change an amount because she knows the duty.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. She still reads the figures, decides, writes and files the budget, and presents it.

reach.task: hear the department budget she presents
reach.learn: The budget is one she wrote from figures she read, not a generated total.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: she still reads the figures, decides the amounts, writes and files budget v1, and presents it. No tool is added.

assumptions: The upkeep allowance is zero because no tool is added.
This performance is one department budget for the year. One episode is that budget.
She writes budget v1 herself. The writing step is not gated. On the file step she checks that budget v1 states the amounts she chose. Filing is internal.
Upper management and the other stakeholders in this episode are inside the organisation. The presentation is spoken. No budget is sent outside, so the presentation is not gated.
She still opens and reads last year's budgets. No listing replaces that reading. No alert is raised.
unknowns: Whether a stakeholder outside the company hears this budget on another task.
research_questions: Who may change budget v1 after she has presented it.

incremental.description: No upkeep, because no tool is added to this task.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: On one department budget she reads last year's figures, decides the amounts, writes budget v1, files it, and presents it to upper management, and none of those steps is shorter, so the saving stays at zero.
